assessmentSummary.identity: Unresolved legacy label. The source permits either a standing or seated base and does not declare grip, support, how the dumbbells reach lockout, whether the concentric press is part of each repetition, assistance, or a safe pickup and set-down cycle.
currentCardFindings: The instruction says to stand or sit, which crosses an established definition boundary.
The instruction begins with dumbbells locked out and says to reset each repetition, but never defines whether the athlete presses, receives assistance, or performs an eccentric-only handoff.
Grip, bench support, rack, pickup, set-down, spotting, load adjustment, and failure response are missing.
The 4–6-second lower is a useful authored tempo constraint, but it cannot repair the missing base and repetition cycle.
Three healthy title-level candidates expose standing-or-unspecified and seated interpretations; none resolves the source contract or creates a human decision.
assessmentSummary.difficultyDecision: Do not score exercise complexity or physical difficulty because the source does not define one executable exercise. Athlete skill or proficiency is excluded as well.
assessmentSummary.loadFatigueDecision: Do not authorize load, fatigue, recovery, or cumulative budgets until base, full repetition cycle, assistance, range, and equipment operations are declared.
assessmentSummary.dosageDecision: Archive the source as nonprescribable. Its authored 4–6-second lowering idea is represented only by separately explicit review-state standing and seated variants.

currentCardSnapshot.description: Dumbbell Overhead Press Eccentric is a slow negative/eccentric drill for overhead press lowering and trunk control. It uses deliberate lowering, clean alignment, and enough rest to build control and tissue capacity without chasing fatigue.
